## usePagination()

<span class="api-kind">function</span>

```ts
declare function usePagination(doc: PageableDocument, options?: PaginationOptions): Pagination;
```

The paging state of a query document, for a pager -- the grid's, or one an application builds.

    const paging = usePagination(foos)

    <button disabled={ paging.page === 0 } onClick={ () => paging.goTo(paging.page - 1) }>Previous</button>

Reads offset, page size and row count from the document and writes through update(), and holds nothing of its
own. The page size is the one in the document's config: where the type's `maxPageSize` held a request to less,
that is the size shown.

**Parameters**

| | |
|---|---|
| `doc` | query document snapshot; its query has to select `rowCount` |
| `options` | page sizes to offer |

## Pagination

<span class="api-kind">interface</span>

```ts
interface Pagination
```

The paging state of a query document, and the ways to change it.

### Pagination.page

```ts
page: number;
```

### Pagination.pageCount

```ts
pageCount: number;
```

### Pagination.pageSize

```ts
pageSize: number;
```

### Pagination.pageSizes

```ts
pageSizes: number[];
```

Page sizes to offer: the options, held to the type's `maxPageSize`, plus the current page size where it isn't
one of them, so a control always has the current size to show.

### Pagination.goTo

```ts
goTo(page: number): Promise<void>;
```

Goes to the page with the given index, held to the pages there are. Does nothing on the current page.

### Pagination.setPageSize

```ts
setPageSize(pageSize: number): Promise<void>;
```

Changes the page size, keeping the first row shown on the page shown. Does nothing on the current size.

## Pager()

<span class="api-kind">function</span>

```ts
declare function Pager({ doc, pageSizes, radius, align, className }: PagerProps): JSX.Element;
```

First, previous, nearby page numbers, next and last page, and a page size select, for any query document.

Built on usePagination() and nothing else, so a pager that has to look different is written the same way.

## PagerProps

<span class="api-kind">type</span>

```ts
type PagerProps = PaginationOptions & {
  /**
   * Query document snapshot to page. Its query has to select `type`, `config` and `rowCount`.
   */
  doc: PageableDocument;
  /**
   * Page numbers to list on either side of the current one. Default 2.
   */
  radius?: number;
  /**
   * Where the pager sits in its row. Default "start".
   */
  align?: "start" | "center" | "end";
  /**
   * Added to the pager's own classes.
   */
  className?: string;
};
```

:::note[Undocumented]
This export carries no doc comment in the source.
:::

## pageCount()

<span class="api-kind">function</span>

```ts
declare function pageCount(rowCount: number, pageSize: number): number;
```

Number of pages the rows take up. At least 1, so an empty result is one empty page and not none.

**Parameters**

| | |
|---|---|
| `rowCount` | total number of rows, as in a document's `rowCount` |
| `pageSize` | rows per page, 0 for all |

## pageSizeOptions()

<span class="api-kind">function</span>

```ts
declare function pageSizeOptions(options: readonly number[], maxPageSize?: number): number[];
```

The page sizes a control can offer given the type's `maxPageSize` from `config().meta`.

Without a limit the options come back as they are. With one, sizes above it are dropped and so is 0 ("all rows"),
which the server would cap too, and the limit itself is added last in their place. What is left keeps the order it
was given in.

**Parameters**

| | |
|---|---|
| `options` | page sizes to offer, 0 for "all rows" |
| `maxPageSize` | the type's largest page, absent for no limit |

## pageWindow()

<span class="api-kind">function</span>

```ts
declare function pageWindow(page: number, pageCount: number, radius?: number): number[];
```

The page indexes a pager lists as numbers: the current page and up to `radius` pages on either side of it. Near
either end the window shifts so it still holds `2 * radius + 1` pages where there are that many.

**Parameters**

| | |
|---|---|
| `page` | current page index, from 0 |
| `pageCount` | number of pages, as from `pageCount()` |
| `radius` | pages to list on either side of the current one |

## useSort()

<span class="api-kind">function</span>

```ts
declare function useSort(doc: SortableDocument, key: FieldExpression): SortState;
```

The sort state of one sort key -- a column header's, or any other control's that sorts by one thing.

Reads the document's config and writes it through update(), and holds nothing of its own: whatever set the sort,
this shows it.

    const sort = useSort(foos, "name")

    <button onClick={ sort.toggle }>
        Name { sort.direction === "asc" ? "▲" : sort.direction === "desc" ? "▼" : "" }
    </button>

The key is a field path (`"owner.name"`) or a FilterDSL expression node. A key naming a direction (`"!name"`,
`desc(...)`) is a mistake: the direction is what toggle() changes.

**Parameters**

| | |
|---|---|
| `doc` | query document snapshot |
| `key` | what to sort by |

## SortableDocument

<span class="api-kind">interface</span>

```ts
interface SortableDocument
```

What useSort() needs of a query document: its config and update(). A snapshot from useInjection() or
useQueryDocument() is one as long as its query selects `config`.

### SortableDocument.config

```ts
config: QueryConfig;
```

### SortableDocument.update

```ts
update(delta: QueryConfigDelta): Promise<unknown>;
```

## SortState

<span class="api-kind">interface</span>

```ts
interface SortState
```

Where one sort key stands in a document's sort order, and the way to sort by it.

### SortState.direction

```ts
direction: SortDirection | null;
```

Direction the document sorts by the key in, `null` if its sort order doesn't name the key.

### SortState.position

```ts
position: number | null;
```

Index of the key in the sort order, 0 for the most significant field, `null` if the order doesn't name the
key. Above 0 only where something other than a header click set a sort of several fields.

### SortState.toggle

```ts
toggle(): Promise<void>;
```

Sorts the document by the key alone: ascending, or descending if the document sorts by the key ascending and
by nothing else. Goes back to the first page, since the rows on any other page are different ones now.

**Returns** the update's promise, settled when the document holds the new rows

## SortHeader()

<span class="api-kind">function</span>

```ts
declare function SortHeader({ doc, sortKey, children, className }: SortHeaderProps): JSX.Element;
```

A table header cell that sorts the document by its key when clicked, and shows where the key stands in the
document's sort order: its direction, and its position where the order has more than one field.

Built on useSort() and nothing else, so a header that has to look different, or isn't a table cell, is written
the same way.

## SortHeaderProps

<span class="api-kind">type</span>

```ts
type SortHeaderProps = {
  /**
   * Query document snapshot to sort. Its query has to select `config`.
   */
  doc: SortableDocument;
  /**
   * What the column sorts by: a field path or a FilterDSL expression node, without a direction.
   */
  sortKey: FieldExpression;
  /**
   * The heading.
   */
  children?: ReactNode;
  /**
   * Added to the header cell's own classes.
   */
  className?: string;
};
```

:::note[Undocumented]
This export carries no doc comment in the source.
:::
